metadata.title: E191 Four AI Semiconductor Frontiers: Tech, Opportunity, and Hype | David × Fang Liang
metadata.guest_role: Strategy Director, Xinglv Intelligent (yield software + inspection)

conclusion: Fang Liang unpacks four hot semiconductor themes — metalens, glass substrate, hybrid bonding, and SiC — via restore-the-facts → 3–5y industry view → investment logic (not stock tips). Metalens is metasurface optics with early phone-CIS examples but incomplete big-OEM adoption; glass substrate wins on CTE/stiffness vs organic substrates, with volume origin ~2026 and product use later — Rubin-glass rumors get cold water; hybrid bonding rides advanced packaging; SiC ranks as the most commercializable of the four, with many domestic players still stuck climbing 6″→8″/12″.
background:
Ep.191, hosted by David, brings back Fang Liang (first on ep.26 in Mar 2024). He has left VC for a semiconductor startup — Xinglv Intelligent — as strategy director, selling yield-management software and inspection gear to fabs and OSATs.

The framing: the industry is drowning in buzzwords, some fake, some stretched. Three goals — explain each tech and puncture rumors; build a mid-term industry view; clarify investment logic and watchpoints without recommending stocks or price targets.
important_facts: Metalens (metasurface optics): collapses lens function into ultra-thin structures that can couple to CIS; industry narrative includes a Xiaomi phone front-camera CIS example, while Apple and peers have not fully adopted — route and yield still unfinished. Thinner form factor and optical degrees of freedom vs traditional lenses; materials/process and system integration constrain scale.

Glass substrate and hybrid bonding: the market's 'glass substrate' usually means glass for FCBGA-class substrates — better CTE/stiffness than organic BT/core for advanced packaging. Volume 'origin' ~2026; real product penetration may slip to 2027+. Treat claims that a whole GPU generation is already on glass with skepticism. Hybrid bonding is a core advanced-packaging interconnect path tied to TSMC-ecosystem roadmaps.

SiC: clearest commercialization path of the four — power devices meet EV/industrial demand; substrate inch climb (6″→8″→12″, PVT growth, etc.) is the industry story. Many domestic makers still on 6″; finance often underweights substrate yield and ramp tempo. Examples are not advice; tech names are volatile.

mental_model.name: Facts First × 3–5y Industry Clock × Logic Not Tips
mental_model.components: Define the physics and stage, map domestic/overseas players and disruption points, then mark mid-checkpoints to track. Separate volume origin from product penetration to catch narrative bubbles. Rank by commercialization maturity to set research priority, not theme trading.
mental_model.application: For advanced packaging, split glass-substrate and hybrid-bonding customer-import calendars; for metalens, track CIS penetration and big-OEM design-ins; for SiC, watch inch nodes and yield, not just domestic listing counts. Use Fang's yield-tool seat as a leading indicator of process ramps.

key_insights.view: Restore the four nouns before pricing the hype.
key_insights.question: Where does the market err?
key_insights.answer: Metalens, glass substrate, hybrid bonding, and SiC get bundled as one 'AI semi' theme. Fang insists on physics and stage first, then a 3–5y view — otherwise lab progress gets priced as volume.

key_insights.view: Glass substrate is a clock problem, not a binary.
key_insights.question: How to read glass narratives?
key_insights.answer: CTE/stiffness advantages are real, but volume origin ~2026 and product use later; treating unproven full-generation glassification as fact is rumor territory.

key_insights.view: SiC is the most commercial; inch climb decides winners.
key_insights.question: How to rank research?
key_insights.answer: Among the four, SiC has the clearest demand and process path; many China players remain on 6″ — differentiation is 8″/12″ yield and capacity, fit for mid-horizon industry tracking.

top_investment_implications.thesis: Hybrid bonding and glass-substrate import calendars ultimately clear through TSMC-ecosystem customer roadmaps — Long the advanced-packaging line only after import timing and yield data confirm, not the theme headline
Guest's yield-management software/hardware firm serves fabs/OSATs — new materials and nodes (glass, SiC, bonding) raise yield-tool demand; private name as an industry observation anchor

golden_quotes: Restore the facts, then give a three-to-five-year industry view.
Among the four, SiC still has the strongest commercialization path.
